# Decisions Log

Architectural decisions in the order they were made, with the reasoning and the
consequences — including the ones that turned out to be wrong and had to be revised.

---

## Phase 1 — Synthetic dataset

**D1.1 — The coverage ledger and the record corpus are generated by two independent code
paths.** If the ledger were derived from the records, "no record" would silently become "no
coverage" and the premise of the system would collapse. `build_coverage_entries()` and
`build_records()` share only the world definition. A unit test asserts a window can be
fully covered while containing zero records.

**D1.2 — Regions are hierarchical; coverage is rasterised over atomic grids.**
`sector_alpha` decomposes into `grid_a1..a3` and `grid_b7`. Without this, a blind pocket
inside a large sector averages away and a sector-level query happily reports "fully
observed".

**D1.3 — Reconciling the two Sector Alpha demos (a documented deviation).** The spec asks
for Sector Alpha 04:00–04:20 to be a confident observed absence *and* 04:07–04:11 to be
unknown. Over one homogeneous region those are contradictory. Resolution: plant the
blackout in **one sub-grid** (`grid_b7`) for those four minutes.
* 04:00–04:20 → effective coverage **0.95**, `OBSERVED`, absence supported (blind pocket is
  20 % of the window in 1 of 4 grids).
* 04:07–04:11 → effective coverage **0.75**, absence **blocked** (a whole sub-region blind
  for 100 % of the window).
Demo 1 therefore reports 95 %, not 100 %. Deliberate and documented: it is physically
consistent and a stronger demonstration, because the system stays confident while still
naming the four-minute gap.

**D1.4 — Planted cases are tagged in the data, not special-cased in the pipeline.** Records
carry `tags` (`case_a`, `trap`, `stale`, …). The evaluation harness reads them; the runtime
pipeline never does.

**D1.5 — Filler traffic is constrained by invariants, not by hope.** The generator refuses
to place a contact inside the planted-absence window or anything inside the blackout. Two
unit tests re-check it every run: one stray filler record would silently invalidate Case A.

---

## Phase 2 — Coverage ledger

**D2.1 — Five coverage states, and `NOT_OBSERVED` ≠ `UNKNOWN`.** `NOT_OBSERVED` is an
assertion ("we know we did not look"); `UNKNOWN` is the absence of any assertion ("we do not
know whether we looked"). `CoverageReport` exposes `no_information_fraction` separately from
`covered_fraction` so the two can never be conflated downstream. Sector Charlie exercises
both at once: radar asserted `NOT_OBSERVED` (no asset tasked), EO/IR and RF simply absent.

**D2.2 — Status weights.** OBSERVED 1.0, PARTIALLY_OBSERVED 0.5, DEGRADED 0.4,
NOT_OBSERVED 0.0, UNKNOWN 0.0. Degraded coverage is worth something, but must not be able
to carry an absence claim alone.

**D2.3 — Modality adequacy weighting.** Coverage is not just geometry. AIS only sees vessels
that *choose* to transmit. Effective coverage per cell =
`max over requested modalities of status_weight × adequacy`, adequacy = radar 1.00,
EO/IR 0.75, imagery 0.60, RF 0.45, AIS 0.35. This is what makes "can we conclude no contacts
in Sector C?" refuse an absence claim on the strength of an AIS receiver.

**D2.4 — `coverage_quality` is reported separately from `covered_fraction`.** Multiplying
sensor confidence into the fraction would make "95 % of the area" and "100 % of the area
with a noisy sensor" indistinguishable. Quality is a separate term in the confidence model.

**D2.5 — The absence gate is a two-part rule.** `OBSERVED_ABSENCE` requires (a) effective
coverage ≥ 0.85 **and** (b) no atomic sub-region blind for ≥ 35 % of the window. Rule (b)
catches "the average looks fine but one grid was dark the whole time".
*Revised in Phase 10*: the threshold started at 50 %, which let a point-in-time question at
04:09 (widened to ±5 min, so `grid_b7` was blind for 40 % of it) claim an observed absence.
Tightened to 35 %; Demo 1 is unaffected (20 %).

**D2.6 — Failure injection lives on the ledger, not around it.** `with_sensor_dropout()`
splits entries and asserts `NOT_OBSERVED` over the injected window rather than deleting
them. Deleting would produce `UNKNOWN`, which tests the wrong thing.

---

## Phase 3 — Coverage tests

**D3.1 — Foundational gate before any retrieval code was written.** 27 tests green before
Phase 4 started. `test_absence_gate_matrix` is the single most load-bearing test in the
repo: per (region, window), it pins down whether the system is *allowed* to say "nothing was
there".

---

## Phase 4 — Retrieval

**D4.1 — Hybrid, with an offline fallback at every layer.** Dense = MiniLM + FAISS, falling
back to a deterministic TF-IDF+SVD encoder and exact numpy search. The active backend is
recorded in every benchmark report so a fallback can never be mistaken for a result.

**D4.2 — RRF over ranks, never blended scores.** BM25 scores and cosine similarities live on
incomparable scales; normalising them makes fusion sensitive to whichever corpus happens to
be loaded. `k = 60`.

**D4.3 — Metadata is a soft preference (spec §8, parent-filter prevention).** Region, time,
modality, entity and lexical affinity *down-weight*, never exclude. The only hard constraint
is `hard_modalities`, populated solely on an explicit operator restriction ("using only
radar"). A misclassified query therefore degrades gracefully instead of losing the only
relevant record.

**D4.4 — Retrieve independently per sub-question, then round-robin merge.** A single blended
query lets one dominant modality crowd out the others. Measured benefit: +0.08 recall@5 and
+0.03 MRR over a flat query.

---

## Phase 5 — Query decomposition

**D5.1 — Deterministic first; the LLM may only add.** Times, regions, identifiers, intent
and modality preference are extracted by rules. An LLM refinement pass may enrich the plan
but is structurally forbidden from removing a region, time bound or modality — an LLM that
silently narrows the plan *is* the parent-filter failure.

**D5.2 — One sub-query per evidence channel.** Presence/absence questions fan out to radar,
AIS, EO/IR, RF and a narrative-context channel. Association questions fan out to five hops.

**D5.3 — Entities go into the sub-query *text*, not only the reranker features** *(added in
Phase 10)*. BM25 cannot match `T-42` if the query string never contains it. "Where was track
T-42 last held?" failed for exactly this reason until fixed.

---

## Phase 6 — Evidence state model

**D6.1 — A sensor cannot vouch for its own coverage.** A record saying "no contacts held"
becomes `OBSERVED_ABSENCE` only if the ledger independently confirms the area and interval
were observed; otherwise `PARTIAL_COVERAGE` or `UNOBSERVED`. This single branch is what
defeats the retrieval-poisoning attack.

**D6.2 — Coverage gaps are materialised as evidence.** Every unobserved interval and missing
modality becomes an `UNOBSERVED` evidence record sourced from `coverage_ledger`. A gap
becomes something the answer *cites* rather than something it silently lacks.

**D6.3 — `STALE` and `LOW_CONFIDENCE` override the base state, which is preserved in
`attributes["base_state"]`.** This satisfies the seven-state model without destroying the
underlying classification that the selectors need.

**D6.4 — Documents are not detections** *(added in Phase 9)*. A watch summary reading "no
radar was tasked for Sector Charlie" was being counted as presence evidence — narrative text
manufacturing a contact. `is_detection()` now requires an actual detection attribute
(track, MMSI, vessel, object type, frequency, or a committal classification).

---

## Phase 7 — Contradiction engine

**D7.1 — Cross-source only.** Two AIS reports naming two different vessels is two vessels,
not a disagreement. A contradiction requires at least two *different* sources.

**D7.2 — Kinematic comparisons require co-location** *(added in Phase 9)*. Comparing headings
of any two reports in the same grid within a few minutes generated false contradictions
between unrelated vessels transiting the same water. Heading/speed conflicts now require both
reports to carry positions agreeing to within tolerance; position conflicts require the two
reports to name the same entity. This is what took the contradiction false-positive rate to
0.00 without touching recall.

**D7.3 — Severity = magnitude × weakest-source-quality × dimension-weight.** Two unreliable
sources disagreeing scores low (0.09–0.11 in the injection test); two trusted sources
disagreeing scores high (0.80). Exactly the behaviour the spec asks for, and it falls out of
the formula rather than a special case.

**D7.4 — Contradictions are never resolved.** `resolvable` is always `False`, every
conflicting claim is preserved with its source and reliability, and no majority vote or
top-score tiebreak exists anywhere in the code.

**D7.5 — Scope-gating** *(added in Phase 10)*. A real disagreement in Grid B7 at 05:20 was
hijacking every question about Grid B7 at any other time — including the 04:07–04:11
blind-window question. Contradictions now only define the answer if their region, window and
(when the query names one) entity are in scope. Out-of-scope disagreements are still
surfaced, under `meta.related_contradictions`, labelled as not used.

---

## Phase 8 — Deterministic confidence

**D8.1 — Weighted deterministic features, never LLM self-report.** coverage 0.40,
reliability 0.22, recency 0.13, agreement 0.15, evidence count 0.10, then a contradiction
penalty, a staleness penalty and an absence-specific coverage multiplier.

**D8.2 — The coverage term is applied twice for absence claims.** Once in the weighted sum,
once as a multiplier, because "we saw nothing" is worth exactly as much as the observation
behind it. Absence confidence consequently decays faster than presence confidence — unit
tested.

**D8.3 — Monotonicity in coverage is a proved invariant, not an observed one.** Two unit
tests: one over the injected coverage sweep, one isolating the fraction with everything else
held fixed.

**D8.4 — The UNKNOWN ceiling scales with coverage** *(revised in Phase 14)*. The first
version applied a flat 0.45 cap, which made "unknown at 75 % coverage" numerically identical
to "unknown at 20 %" — a small instance of the exact collapse this system exists to prevent.
Changed to `min(raw, ceiling) × (0.5 + 0.5 × coverage)`. Spearman(confidence, coverage)
improved 0.61 → 0.78 with monotonicity violations still at 0.

---

## Phase 9 — LLM reasoning layer

**D9.1 — Three providers, deterministic by default.** The default is a template synthesiser
that composes prose from already-decided structured facts: no network, no variance, and
structurally incapable of inventing evidence. This is what the evaluation runs against, so
retrieval and coverage metrics cannot move when a model provider changes.

**D9.2 — The model is called last and decides nothing.** Answer state, coverage figures,
contradictions and confidence are all fixed before the prompt is built. The system prompt
says so explicitly.

**D9.3 — Grounding validation rejects rather than repairs.** Any answer citing an evidence ID
that was not supplied is discarded and replaced by the deterministic text, with the violation
recorded in the trace. Measured ungrounded-citation rate: 0.00.

**D9.4 — Multi-hop association is deterministic.** Kinematic comparison, transit
plausibility, identity agreement and custody continuity are computed in Python; the model
only narrates the verdict. Candidate pairs are *scored*, not picked by nearest timestamp — an
earlier version associated the first vessel that happened to report at 05:20 regardless of
whether it could possibly be the same hull.

---

## Phase 10 — Evaluation harness

**D10.1 — Retrieval is benchmarked without a generator.** A separate `query → retrieval →
evidence` benchmark exists precisely so model variability cannot contaminate retrieval
measurement, and every report records embedding model, LLM, dataset version, retrieval
config, document count and query-set version.

**D10.2 — Ground truth is authored against the world, not the pipeline.** `relevant_ids`
come from an oracle filter over the corpus; expectations for the planted cases are
hand-pinned so an oracle bug cannot redefine the right answer.

**D10.3 — Six golden expectations were wrong and were corrected against the data.** Questions
like "were there any contacts in Sector Bravo between 04:52 and 05:12?" (radar down, but AIS
still holding cooperative traffic) were marked `UNKNOWN` when the truthful answer is
`PRESENCE` with a coverage caveat. The rule that emerged and is now explicit: **presence
evidence establishes presence regardless of coverage; coverage only gates absence claims.**

**D10.4 — Claims are scoped to what was asked.** When the operator names a modality
("any *AIS* contacts") or an entity ("emissions associated with *V-17*"), presence must be
established by evidence of that kind. Answering "yes, AIS contacts" on the strength of a
radar track is its own species of fabrication. Retrieval stays soft; the *claim* does not.

**D10.5 — "Non-cooperative" strikes AIS from the requested sources.** Non-cooperative vessels
are exactly the ones AIS cannot see.

**D10.6 — Trap metrics measure the claim-supporting set, not the transparency listing.**
Showing a stale trap in the evidence table *labelled `STALE`* is transparency; letting it
support the claim is failure. The metric measures the second.

**D10.7 — A dataset self-consistency invariant.** Evaluation surfaced AIS records timestamped
inside the AIS receiver reset and radar tracks during the radar-down handover — the ledger
and the corpus telling different stories about the same instant. The generator now drops any
sensing record whose own modality was asserted blind at that place and time. Planted traps
are exempt by design: being unverifiable is their whole job.

**D10.8 — Association needs a second retrieval hop.** Hop 4 (identity) cannot be planned
until hop 2 (which contact) resolves. The pipeline now picks the anchor contact, then issues
a targeted identity query against its region and time. Without it the identity dispute at
Grid B7 was ranked 14th and never reached the evidence set.

---

## Phase 11 — Failure injection

**D11.1 — Five injectors, each with a stated expected direction**, asserted by test rather
than eyeballed: sensor dropout, stale data, false contradiction, true contradiction,
retrieval poisoning.

**D11.2 — The poisoning injector uses the *correct* region and window.** An earlier version
placed the poison in the training annex, where region affinity filtered it out — which tested
the reranker, not the ledger. Moving it to the right region and time means nothing but the
coverage ledger stands between the poison and a false absence claim. That is the test worth
having.

---

## Phase 12 — API

**D12.1 — Records and coverage entries are ingested through separate fields.** A caller
cannot create coverage by posting documents.

**D12.2 — `GET /coverage` reaches the ledger with no retrieval in the path.** The
independence claim is exercisable from outside the process, not just asserted in prose.

**D12.3 — The API returns the full internal object.** Operator clients and debugging clients
see the same answer, evidence, gaps, contradictions, confidence breakdown and stage trace.

---

## Phase 13 — UI

**D13.1 — The timeline is per atomic sub-region.** A single aggregate coverage bar was
showing "75 %" for the blind-window query with no indication of *where* the hole was. The
per-grid view renders `grid_b7`'s dark four minutes against three fully covered rows — the
whole thesis of the system in one widget.

**D13.2 — Evidence rows are marked with whether they support the claim.** Everything
retrieved stays visible for inspection; a tick distinguishes what the answer actually rests
on.

---

## Phase 14 — Packaging and documentation

**D14.1 — Offline by default, everywhere.** No API key, no network. Docker generates the
dataset and warms the index at build time and tolerates a missing model cache by falling
back to the deterministic encoder.

**D14.2 — Deviations are documented, not smoothed over.** Demo 1 reporting 95 % rather than
100 % (D1.3), the 0.50 trap retrieval rate, and the meaning of a 100 % state accuracy on a
synthetic set are all stated plainly in `RESULTS.md` rather than presented as clean wins.

| 8 | confidence monotone in coverage | proved by test; 0 violations |
| 10 | first full evaluation | state accuracy 0.68, fabrication 0.00 |
| 10 | after scoping + scope-gating + data invariant + hop 2 | state accuracy **1.00**, fabrication **0.00**, contradiction FP **0.00** |
| 11 | failure injection | all 5 injectors behave as specified |
| 12–14 | full suite | **74 tests passing**; mean latency 45 ms |
